issues.body: term_to_ntriples fails closed only for invalid literal language/direction metadata. The `bnode` branch appends term.value after `_:` without validating the blank-node-label grammar, while the catch-all branch returns term.value verbatim whenever triple is absent. TermRef is public and Deserialize, so an edited value such as `{"kind":"triple","value":"attacker-controlled SPARQL"}` reaches DELETE/INSERT syntax unchanged. Unknown kinds take the same branch. This contradicts the new all-or-nothing safety contract and leaves an executable injection path.
issues.fix_hint: Make serialization accept only the explicit kinds `iri`, `bnode`, `literal`, and `triple`; reject unknown kinds. For `triple`, require structured components and recursively serialize them (or parse and validate the carried text as exactly one RDF triple term before re-emitting it). Validate blank-node labels against the applicable N-Triples grammar before emission. Add malicious deserialization tests for an opaque triple value, an unknown kind, and a punctuation-bearing blank-node label, each proving that no update is emitted.
issues.title: Deserialized term kinds and blank-node labels still permit SPARQL injection

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes both prior findings: language/direction metadata is now validated with all-or-nothing update construction, and the computed-field test asserts the exact default and feature-enabled results. However, the same public, deserializable TermRef still has other unvalidated serialization branches: arbitrary/"triple" kinds without structured components are copied verbatim, and blank-node labels are emitted verbatim. Either can place attacker-controlled SPARQL syntax into an update. Because this is a new major finding despite resolution of the old findings, progress is regressing under the required scale.
